title: What Does the Bible Say About Adultery? 28 Verses
description: What the Bible says about adultery: the seventh commandment, Jesus on lust and divorce, the woman caught in adultery and David's sin, in full.
keywords: what does the bible say about adultery
summary: Adultery appears in 34 verses of the World English Bible and adulterer in 12. It is banned in the seventh commandment (Exodus 20:14), carried the death penalty in the Law (Leviticus 20:10), is described by Proverbs as destroying the one who commits it (Proverbs 6:32) and is used by the prophets as a picture of Israel's unfaithfulness to God (Jeremiah 3:8). Jesus widens the command to include lust in the heart (Matthew 5:27-28), treats remarriage after divorce as a form of adultery except for sexual immorality (Matthew 19:9), and shows mercy to a woman caught in adultery (John 8:3-11). David's adultery with Bathsheba and his repentance (2 Samuel 11-12, Psalm 51) show the pattern of sin, confrontation and forgiveness.

faqs.q: Is adultery forgiven in the Bible?
faqs.a: Yes, on repentance. Jesus tells the woman caught in adultery 'neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more' (John 8:11), and David is forgiven after confessing (2 Samuel 12:13, Psalm 51). Paul lists adulterers among those outside the kingdom, then adds 'such were some of you' (1 Corinthians 6:9-11).

faqs.q: Is lust the same as adultery?
faqs.a: Jesus says that everyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her in his heart (Matthew 5:28). He is saying the commandment reaches the heart; he is not saying a thought has the same consequences as an act.

faqs.q: Does the Bible allow divorce for adultery?
faqs.a: Jesus permits divorce for sexual immorality (Matthew 5:32, 19:9) and says that marrying a divorced person otherwise is adultery. Christians differ on how widely to apply the exception and on remarriage.

faqs.q: What does the seventh commandment say?
faqs.a: 'You shall not commit adultery' (Exodus 20:14, Deuteronomy 5:18). Under the Law adultery meant sex with another man's wife and was punishable by death for both (Leviticus 20:10). The New Testament applies it to both spouses (Mark 10:11-12).
